items.note: Quote and text are verbatim from L25 and unchanged. Outcomes match the two stated conditions (name-contains-term, caption). The added 'regardless of letter case' clause is explicitly attributed to gap G7 rather than stated as bare fact, and G7 itself is grounded (see G7). Layer 'ui' is correct: this criterion mentions only web-shop behaviour, no API.

Quote and text are verbatim from L26. Outcomes (200, name-contains-term case-insensitive, PLIERS/pliers equivalence) all restate the sentence with no addition. Layer 'api' is correct (criterion is API-only).

Quote and text verbatim from L27. All four outcomes (UI message, 200, empty data, total 0) map 1:1 to the sentence, nothing invented (no current_page/last_page values are asserted). Layer 'e2e' is correct since the same sentence describes both web shop and API.
Quote/text verbatim from L28; outcomes restate ascending price on both web shop and GET /products?sort=price,asc. Layer 'e2e' correct.

Quote/text verbatim from L29; outcomes restate 'only hammers' / 'only products in that category'. GET /categories/tree is listed as a supporting endpoint for this AC, consistent with G3 (L35) which is the documented way to obtain the Hammer id; this doesn't add a new asserted condition. Layer 'e2e' correct.

Quote/text verbatim from L30. Outcomes unpack 'paginated ... 12 per page (per_page 12)' into per_page=12 plus 'at most 12, exactly 12 unless last page' for both web shop and API; this is the direct arithmetic meaning of per_page-based pagination, not an added condition. Associating the rule with both GET /products and GET /products/search is reasonable since L21 shows both return per_page/current_page/last_page and L30 says 'in the API' without naming one endpoint. Layer 'e2e' correct.

Quote/text verbatim from L31. The outcome operationalises 'returns all products' as total-equals-GET-/products-total, which is the only literal reading of 'all products' given the response shape at L21; the real ambiguities (q= vs q omitted; status code) are correctly pushed out to G5/G6 rather than silently assumed. Layer 'api' correct (no UI mentioned).
Text is the verbatim last sentence of L19: 'The web shop and the public catalogue API (used by our mobile app) must behave the same way.' No change of meaning.

Faithful paraphrase of L21: both endpoints return the stated shape, and 'GET /products is paginated' matches the parenthetical that attaches 'paginated' only to /products in the source. No overreach (does not claim /products/search is explicitly called 'paginated' in the text).

L31 ('An empty search (no term)') genuinely does not say whether q is sent empty or omitted, and L21/L26 only ever show the form q=<term>. The gap is correctly labelled 'assumed' (not overclaimed as found), and the contract does not silently pick a variant elsewhere without flagging it.
L31 states no status code for the empty-search case, while L26/L27 do state 200 for the term-search and no-match cases respectively; correctly left 'open' rather than assumed.

L25 is indeed silent on case-sensitivity for the web shop. The resolution ('web shop matches regardless of case, like the API') is a direct application of the explicit parity rule at L19 ('must behave the same way') to the explicit API behaviour at L26, so it is grounded in cited source lines rather than general assumption, even though it required combining two lines rather than a single verbatim statement.
"GET /products" appears verbatim at L21 with the described parameters and pagination note.
"GET /categories/tree" appears verbatim at L35 as the source of category ids.

observations.note: States 'none: the story calls it the public catalogue API' (story.md#L19). The pack never explicitly says no login/authentication is required; this is inferred from the word 'public'. Reasonable, but flagged since it's an inference dressed as a sourced fact.

States 'none needed: read-only checks ...' and 'cleanup: none (nothing is created)'. The pack never explicitly states the checks are read-only or that no cleanup is needed; this follows from all seven ACs being GET-based, but is not itself asserted anywhere in story.md.

summary: The contract quotes every acceptance criterion, rule and endpoint verbatim from the cited story.md lines with no added or dropped conditions, and its layer classifications match what each criterion describes. The three oracle gaps (G5, G6, G7) correctly identify genuine ambiguities/silences in the source and are labelled with an honest confidence level (assumed / open / found-in-requirement) rather than overclaiming. No requirement-bearing (●) line in the evidence pack is left uncaptured.
